comparator.name: History
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–2027 programme-specific Teaching and Examination Regulations establish a 180-EC History bachelor. Year 1 is 60 EC: A Global History of the Netherlands (5), Ancient World (5), Middle Ages (5), Making of the Modern World 1500–1945 (10), Long 20th Century (10), Historical Research (10), Regions: Introduction (5), and an IMPACT course in Global Changes or Cultural Heritage (10). Year 2 is 60 EC: Sources and Methods (10), three 10-EC research seminars in Political, Cultural, and Social-economic History, Historiography (5), Historical Theory (5), and Regions: Research Seminar (10). Year 3 is a 30-EC minor, Theory of History in Practice (5), Regions: Case Studies (10), Workshop Public History (5), and BA Thesis (10). The published structure therefore accounts for 60 + 60 + 60 = 180 EC without inventing elective content.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Modern History, sociology and Western art history establish chronological, social and visual foundations in semester 1. Histories of Gender, the history of warfare and the Renaissance Mediterranean precede work on empire, modern sociology, Indigenous histories, African heritage and world archaeology. The final year concentrates advanced social theory, museums, race, film, art-historical writing, documentary practice and the History Research Seminar. Every course is available in its assigned term and all formal prerequisites are satisfied.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the generic historical identity, the full six-course UCR History sequence, methods and public-facing cultural history. Groningen formally includes three distinct 10-EC research seminars in Political, Cultural, and Social-economic History. Cultural History is integrated into the closest match; Political History and Social-economic History support two additional feasible directions. All three retain the complete UCR History sequence but diverge substantially in adjacent courses. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both survey modern and contemporary political, social and cultural change; UCR begins in 1815 and is less specifically European.
Both examine historical power and identity across long periods; UCR does so comparatively through empires rather than the programme's broader chronological and regional sequence.

UCR's history of warfare contributes a comparative research-based account of changing power, states and conflict; the Groningen seminar has a broader ancient and medieval regional and global History scope.

Introduction to World Archaeology uses artefacts and material culture to study ancient societies across world regions; Groningen's course is dedicated ancient history and therefore has greater period-specific historical depth.

Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean covers a substantial early-modern European and Mediterranean segment through art, trade and cross-cultural exchange; it is not a full early-modern history survey.
Western art history includes urban, civic and cultural contexts relevant to cities and citizens, but does not reproduce Groningen's dedicated ancient and medieval history course.
UCR has no scheduled course providing the dedicated medieval-history breadth and weight of Groningen's compulsory course.
Research Methods & Statistics supplies research design and quantitative analysis relevant to big-data historical questions, but is not taught as a dedicated digital-history course.
Both teach systematic source collection, interpretation and reflexivity; Groningen applies these skills specifically in a historical research laboratory.
Both develop structured academic argument, evidence use and writing; Groningen's course is specifically historical writing.
Writing Art's Histories explicitly studies historiography and the interpretation of historical scholarship, within art history rather than the full history discipline.
History Research Seminar is UCR's closest scheduled independent historical-research experience and culminates in a substantial paper; it is 7.5 EC and not Groningen's required 10-EC bachelor thesis.
UCR History courses provide comparative and global perspectives, but no scheduled course reproduces the dedicated survey of Dutch history in global context.
UCR courses provide philosophical and social context, but no scheduled course is a dedicated foundations-of-history requirement at Groningen's specified scope.
Groningen's 30-EC minor or approved study-abroad package is genuine open profiling space; no single content is invented or equated to one UCR course.
Groningen preserves a bounded 10-EC choice between Global Changes and Cultural Heritage; no single option is invented or equated to one UCR course.
UCR embeds regional cases across its History courses but has no separate introductory regional-history requirement.
UCR can assemble social and economic history through History, sociology and economics, but it has no dedicated 10-EC Social-economic History research seminar.
UCR uses regional case studies within several courses but has no dedicated 10-EC Regions III course.
Heritage, museums, documentary work and communication support public history, but UCR has no dedicated compulsory Public History workshop.

notes.text: Groningen’s programme is a coherent 180-EC History degree with chronological coverage from the ancient world through the present, compulsory political, cultural and social-economic research seminars, historical methods, theory and historiography, regional research, public history and a BA thesis. UCR offers six History courses and can build strong historical pathways with archaeology, economics, politics, sociology, law, heritage, literature and media, but it does not reproduce that continuous disciplinary sequence or its full research and thesis requirements. These pathways are close or related liberal-arts responses, not substitutes for a full History major.
